summary.text: Celeste Maloy is the Republican U.S. Representative who won re-election on November 3, 2026 in Utah's newly drawn 3rd District, according to unofficial results, after representing the old 2nd District since November 2023.

A Cedar City native and attorney, she worked as a soil conservationist and then in public lands and water law before serving as counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart, whose seat she won in a 2023 special election. She sits on the Appropriations and Natural Resources committees and chairs the Congressional Western Caucus.

paragraphs.text: Celeste Maloy was born in Cedar City, Utah, in 1981, and was raised in Hiko, Nevada, where she graduated from Pahranagat Valley High School.
She earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Southern Utah University in 2003 and a J.D. from Brigham Young University in 2015.
Maloy began her career as a soil conservationist, which her House website says lasted about a decade working with Utah families and farmers.

After law school she worked as a deputy Washington County attorney, a public lands attorney for the Utah Association of Counties and a staff attorney for the Washington County Water Conservancy District.
Maloy served as chief legal counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart before running for his seat.

She won the Republican convention on June 24, 2023, then the September 5, 2023 special Republican primary with 38.8% over Becky Edwards and Bruce Hough, and the November 21, 2023 special general election with 56.8% to succeed Stewart. She took office November 28, 2023.

Maloy was re-elected in November 2024 with 58.0% of the vote over Democrat Nathaniel Woodward. In the 2023-2024 term she served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) Maloy serves on the Committee on Appropriations, as vice chair of the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee and as a member of the Energy and Water Development and Legislative Branch subcommittees. She also serves on the Committee on Natural Resources, on its Federal Lands and Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees.
She chairs the Congressional Western Caucus and, according to her House website, holds co-chair roles on the Bipartisan Build America, Bipartisan Wildfire and other caucuses.
During the campaign, she emphasized tax cuts, border security and giving Utah more control over federal lands.
Maloy won the November 3, 2026 general election with 57.1% of the vote to Kent Udell's 35.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
